title: streaming: lifecycle controls for client-cancel, disconnect handling, reconnect/resume, and server timeout hardening
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: production workloads observed two classes of client-initiated failures: 1) explicit client cancel (via client-side abort/close) which left server-side tasks and KV caches in limbo, increasing memory and token billing; 2) transient network disconnects that should allow reconnect/resume semantics but instead caused duplicated generations or dropped state. Additionally, server-side timeout windows allowed long-running background cleanup to overlap with new reconnect attempts, producing race conditions (tracked in ENG-3421). This PR implements a unified lifecycle control surface for streaming endpoints: (a) explicit client-cancel propagation that aborts generation tasks and triggers immediate KV cache release tied to the request; (b) disconnect handling with a configurable grace period and reconnection token that allows reconnect+resume within N seconds; (c) resume semantics that replay last committed token index and continue generation without duplication; (d) server-side timeout hardening so background cleanup waits for active reconnect windows to close before evicting cached session state. Changes: consolidated control paths in the streaming dispatcher, added a reconnect token handshake for OpenAI-compat streaming clients, introduced a new StreamingSession state machine, and exposed two new API flags: streaming_reconnect_window_ms and streaming_force_cleanup_ms (defaults chosen to be conservative). Also added metrics and traces for lifecycle transitions and instrumented critical paths for SLO observability. Testing: unit tests for state transitions, integration tests simulating client cancel and reconnect across RPC boundaries, e2e canary with synthetic traffic to validate no token duplication and memory stability. CI: flakiness observed on first run due to race in the teardown path; added deterministic teardown ordering and retried CI. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag and rollout to 10% traffic first, validate streaming SLOs and memory footprint, then 100% rollout. Backout: disable runtime flag; cleanup is idempotent. Notes: aligns with OpenAI-compat expectations for reconnect/resume (see discussion in ENG-3510) and requires SDK minor versions to pick up reconnect token handshake (python/ts SDKs PRs queued).
commits: Add StreamingSession state machine and lifecycle transitions
Wire reconnect token handshake into streaming dispatcher
Expose runtime config: streaming_reconnect_window_ms and streaming_force_cleanup_ms
Add unit + integration tests for cancel/disconnect/resume
Instrument metrics and traces for streaming lifecycle
Fix teardown race by serializing cleanup with reconnect window
review_comments: Diego Rivera: Can we avoid holding KV cache locks during the reconnect window? Holding them increased tail latency in a microbenchmark. -- Reply (Maya): Good catch; moved to a best-effort lease model so cache references are weak and cleanup is gated by the reconnect token lifecycle.

Priya Natarajan: Need to be explicit about failure modes for SDKs that never send a reconnect token (mobile clients). Suggest a default small reconnect window and doc note. -- Reply (Maya): Added docs note and set conservative default (5000ms). Mobile clients will fall back to no-resume path after window expires.

Samir Patel: CI flake in teardown reproduced locally; looks like goroutine leak from dispatcher.close -> session.cleanup ordering. Please add a test for goroutine count. -- Reply (Maya): Added goroutine-count assertion in integration test and serialized close/cleanup path.
Diego Rivera: Approve after minor nits fixed on comments and doc wording.
release_notes: Fix streaming lifecycle: properly propagate client cancels, allow reconnect/resume within configurable window, and harden server cleanup timeouts to avoid duplicate tokens and memory leaks.
